correctness.rationale: The derivative c+a*x^2 proves exact discriminant and squarefreeness. The genus-three regular differential basis and direct Cartier identities give a-number one, rank zero for a=0 and rank two for a nonzero. The additive kernel of x^4+b*x^2+c*x yields three separable elliptic quotients; their characteristic-two Artin--Schreier equations have j=0. The three order-two quotient invariant cohomologies exhaust H1, proving the supersingular isogeny; Frobenius orbit block determinants give every L-factor. Exact finite-field verification independently reconstructs all F2 L-series and supersingular orbit factors. No finite computation is elevated to an infinite proof. For the descent census, unordered independent pairs in a two-dimensional F2-subspace count \((q-1)(q-2)/6\) split cubics; rational-root incidences give the mixed pattern \(q(q-1)/2\), and subtraction gives irreducible cubics \((q^2-1)/3\). The checker reproduces all three counts for \(q=2,4,8\).

originality.rationale: The principal proposed original component is the complete Frobenius descent classification (three precise coefficient frequencies) and induced L-factor formula in the monic Picard chart over every Fq, notably the nonrational quotient-involution cases. Nart--Ritzenthaler 2003 already dominate the abstract Newton moduli strata and Nart--Ritzenthaler 2009 Proposition 2.5 literally supplies the supersingular elliptic quotient equations after coefficient specialization; neither is claimed as new. Direct comparison did not reveal the all-q coefficient counting and nonrational-orbit zeta statement in the inspected material. Derivability as a short descent corollary is a substantial residual priority/value risk.
residual_risks: The elliptic quotient equations are already Proposition 2.5 of arXiv:0905.0546; the new Frobenius orbit formula is a natural Galois-descent deduction from established geometry, so it may be an unlocated published corollary or considered routine independently.
Nart--Ritzenthaler 2003/2009 are strong broader coverage: an unnoticed coordinate lemma or a descent corollary may subsume the exact zeta formula.
The full original Bouw paper on p-ranks of tame cyclic covers was not accessible; no whole-document novelty claim about it is made.

value.rationale: The natural supersingular Picard coefficient boundary has exactly three arithmetic descent patterns over every Fq, with exact coefficient counts and a complete induced-orbit genus-three L-polynomial requiring elliptic point counts only over small extensions. The case with no Fq-rational translation subgroup is geometrically natural and arithmetically distinct; the combined exact classification is a nontrivial explicit specialization, not a renamed isolated example. The quotient equations themselves are established Nart--Ritzenthaler results and are attributed.
